title: LinkedIn Cuts Daily Spark Shuffle Fetch Failures from 750 to 20 with Apache Celeborn
gist: LinkedIn moved most Spark and Flink workloads to Apache Celeborn, a disaggregated remote shuffle service, replacing its in-cluster Magnet push-based shuffle; daily shuffle fetch failures fell from ~750 to 20, compute costs dropped 10% and runtimes improved 14%. Hardware and tuning choices (NVMe SSDs, Zstandard over LZ4, 100 Gbps NICs) cut shuffle cost per task nearly 90% and support LinkedIn's shift to a unified Flink architecture.

insights.claim: LinkedIn's deployment of Apache Celeborn as a shared remote shuffle platform across most Spark and Flink workloads cut daily shuffle fetch failures from about 750 to 20, lowered compute costs by 10%, and improved application runtimes by 14% versus its prior Magnet implementation.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Separating shuffle storage from compute yields material cost and reliability gains, a pattern likely to spread across large data platforms.

themes.theme: Reliability engineering of the control plane

insights.claim: LinkedIn runs Celeborn with a five-node Raft-based control plane across availability zones using Apache Ratis, plus network-aware replication and host-health integration that deprioritizes or excludes degraded workers, contributing to a 20-fold reduction in task failures during infrastructure disruptions versus Magnet.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Health-aware scheduling dramatically improves resilience of data pipelines during maintenance.

insights.claim: Moving LinkedIn's shuffle storage to NVMe SSDs reduced overall shuffle duration by 40%.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Dedicated shuffle tiers create incremental demand for NVMe flash in data centers.

insights.claim: Switching shuffle compression from LZ4 to Zstandard reduced LinkedIn's required shuffle worker fleet by about 35%.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Software-level choices like compression can shrink hardware fleets substantially.
insights.locator: LinkedIn further optimized the data plane

insights.claim: With 100 Gbps network interfaces on shuffle workers and JVM and data-plane tuning (sixfold faster slot selection), LinkedIn cut shuffle cost per task by nearly 90% and reduced executor time spent waiting on shuffle by about 10-15% from peak.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: High-bandwidth networking is a key enabler of disaggregated data architectures, supporting data-center networking demand.

insights.claim: LinkedIn's converged Flink platform processes hundreds of millions of events per hour in historical backfills, finishing multi-day workloads in single-digit hours, and thousands of pipelines now use unified Flink computations instead of parallel Spark implementations.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shift from Spark toward unified Flink streaming-plus-batch could favor Flink-centric vendors over Spark-centric ones.
